analysis:
NVDA fell 9.7%, underperforming the market by 5.3 points but tracking closely with its AI compute peers, which posted a median decline of 10.3%. The coverage includes a headline noting the Nasdaq dived 5.5% with Nvidia among the plungers, alongside a broader "post-election reset" in markets; one piece mentions Nvidia's stock is down nearly 24% ahead of earnings, though these are headlines only with no article text available.

The company reports earnings in 12 days, and its history around reports shows a complicated pattern: it has beaten estimates in all eight tracked quarters, yet five of those beats were followed by declines, with a typical abnormal move (beyond what the market explains) of 2.5% in either direction. Most recently in August 2026, a 6.2% earnings beat produced a 7.5 percentage point abnormal gain, but the three reports before that all saw negative abnormal moves despite beats, including drops of 4.3 and 2.1 points in February and May 2026.
